assign.card: Unmerged work: branches built and never merged

findings.text: Every page that draws the In-flight block now fetches `/framework/ai/unmerged.json`, and that file is gitignored and only exists after someone runs `--write` by hand. So the fetch 404s in production and on any dev checkout that hasn't run it (`core/Session/InFlightView.js:255`). `Server/smoke.mjs:44` counts any same-origin fetch 404 as a FAIL, so this breaks the merge gate. Have something always write the file (see 2), or check for it before fetching.

Ask 3, "keep it visible", is only half met: nothing runs `node Server/unmerged.mjs --write` automatically. `core/Session/doc/in-flight.md:40` says "run it on a schedule or by hand", but no schedule exists, so the "Built, not merged" row stays empty or goes stale. Run it from the heartbeat or from `merge.mjs` / `on-landing.mjs`, and say which one in the doc.

The tool picks a branch's owner by finding any `.jsonl` that mentions the branch name (`Server/unmerged.mjs:55-73`). Task logs already record their own branch (`assign.branch`, read by `SessionIndex.reduce` in `Server/LandingCheck.mjs:22-24`). Because of this, audit logs get counted as owners: `unmerged-2026-11-03.json` gives `refine-demo`, `refine-audit` and `undone-to-tasks` to `sessions-and-tasks/deputy/unlanded-worktrees`, and `dictate-plugins` to `chat-settings-per-session`. Those wrong owners then show up in this session's "Built, not merged" row. Look up `assign.branch` first and fall back to a name match only after that (law 6: reuse what exists).

`core/Session/doc/in-flight.md:40` links `/Server/doc/unmerged.md`. `Server/` isn't served by the static site, so that link 404s on the page. Use a repo path in backticks instead, the way other core docs cite `Server/` files.

There are now two "is this branch's work on michael/dev" checks. `on_base` uses `git cherry`, which the brief allowed. `Server/LandingCheck.mjs` (doc `Servex/doc/landing.md`) already answers the same question by file content, and the triage's own "same files" hint repeats that by hand. Consider showing LandingCheck's verdict beside `on_base`, so 17 superseded branches don't need two methods.

`triage.md` adds two buckets the brief didn't ask for: "check" (8 branches) and "older, presumed abandoned" (89). The brief asked for three: merge, superseded and abandoned. The extra buckets are honest, since 89 branches weren't checked one by one, but 89 of 136 aren't triaged into the owner's three words. The counts add up to 136, against the brief's "40". Add one sentence explaining the gap, which is probably the 6-hour/code-only filter.

The test that a log is complete, `/"(finish|complete|landed_at)"/` (`Server/unmerged.mjs:64`), also matches a value such as `"state":"complete"` or `"now":"complete"`. A task can be marked complete by any line that merely quotes the word.
`Server/unmerged.mjs:82` has an indentation slip (four tabs). `unmerged-2026-11-03.json` has no trailing newline.

Can a fresh agent continue from the task folder? Mostly yes. `requirements.md`, `triage.md`, the JSON snapshot and `past-work.md` are there, and both new docs are indexed (`Server/readme.md`, `in-flight.md`). Two things are missing: `session.jsonl` has no log or landing lines yet, and nothing says the worktree is `C:/Code/lew42/worktrees/unmerged-work` (`worktree/unmerged-work`, commit `2a181a161`).

fixed: owners come from each log's own "branch" field (git grep), a text mention no longer owns; test covers it
fixed: relative repo link in in-flight.md
noted: cherry (by patch) vs LandingCheck (by content) can disagree; doc/unmerged.md says so; merging them is a follow-up
noted: the extra buckets exist because 89 branches cannot be judged one by one; triage.md now explains 40 vs 136
fixed: completeness matches only a line starting with a finish/complete verb, or landed_at
fixed: indentation; snapshot json is a record, trailing newline not needed
fixed: triage.md names the worktree path and the tool
